subject: English
passage: When a metal surface is going to be painted, workers must decide when to apply the primer coat. Primer is usually applied to the metal well before the topcoat of paint is added. Applying primer in advance can improve how strongly the paint bonds to the metal, which means the finished surface will resist chipping. But the bonding benefit fades quickly, so workers need to be careful in timing the priming and the painting of a metal surface.
prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the underlined claim?

choices.A: Painters tend to prefer using newer types of primer rather than older formulations.
choices.B: Paint is more likely to bond strongly when the metal surface has been cleaned before priming.
choices.C: Laboratory tests show weak paint adhesion on metal surfaces that were primed a long time before the paint was applied.
choices.D: The kind of primer a worker selects helps determine how strongly the paint will bond to the metal.

explanation: Choice C is the best answer. The underlined claim holds that the bonding benefit of priming fades quickly, so workers must carefully time priming and painting. A finding that laboratory tests show weak paint adhesion on metal surfaces primed a long time before paint was applied would directly support this claim, because it demonstrates that the adhesion benefit diminishes when a long gap separates priming from painting — confirming the need for careful timing.
